about.title: About Me
about.text: Software Engineer with 4 years of experience in full stack development, building scalable applications and robust APIs. Proficient in TypeScript and Python, with a backend focus using FastAPI and Node.js, as well as React on the frontend. Experience building and consuming REST APIs, system integration, and data modeling in relational and non-relational databases, including vector databases for semantic search.
about.text2: Experience with SQL, Python, and BI tools (Power BI, Metabase) for operational and financial indicator analysis. Hands-on with event-driven architectures, Clean Architecture, SOLID, automated testing, CI/CD, and cloud (AWS and Azure). Also develops generative AI solutions (LLMs, RAG, LangChain), including prompt engineering, AI pipelines, and conversational interfaces integrated into real business systems.

ask.title: Ask my portfolio
ask.sub: Conceptual RAG demo. Your question is converted to an embedding, similar chunks are retrieved from my experience vector, and the LLM answers grounded on that context.
ask.q1: How do you use LLMs in production?
ask.q1_chunk1: HR platform with semantic CV scoring via RAG + Azure OpenAI + pgvector.
ask.q1_chunk2: Role-fit evaluation, integration with Totvs/RM and candidate portal.
ask.q1_answer: I use LLMs in production on three main fronts: (1) RAG for semantic CV scoring in the HR platform — Azure OpenAI embeddings stored in pgvector, similarity search against the job description + reranking; (2) a conversational agent (Fictor360 AI) that translates natural-language questions into DAX queries on Power BI via MCP, orchestrated with LangGraph and WebSocket streaming; (3) business-rule validation in approval flows in the super-app. Always with observability, fallbacks, and deterministic tests on the critical paths.
ask.q2_chunk1: Conversational agent that turns questions into DAX and queries Power BI semantic models in real time.
ask.q2_chunk2: LangGraph + Azure OpenAI + Power BI MCP, WebSocket streaming.
ask.q2_answer: Fictor360 AI is an agent that talks to Power BI. Pipeline: user asks in natural language → the agent loads the full semantic model profile (tables, measures, relationships) as context → LangGraph orchestrates: generate DAX, validate via MCP, execute, interpret result → response streams back over WebSocket. The model profile grounds the LLM's reasoning and dramatically cuts hallucination on measure names. Stack: NestJS, LangGraph, Azure OpenAI, Power BI MCP server, DAX.
ask.q3_chunk1: Python pipelines, ETL with Pandas, dashboards on Metabase and Power BI.
ask.q3_chunk2: RPA with Selenium for data extraction from legacy ERP without an API.
ask.q3_answer: I started at Atalaia turning manual processes into automation: RPA in Python + Selenium to scrape a legacy ERP without an API (~70% drop in collection time), ETL pipelines with Pandas, Metabase deployment with 10+ dashboards. At Fictor I evolved into Power BI integration via REST/MCP, semantic modeling, and embedded BI with Azure AD RLS. SQL is my Swiss army knife — from production queries to exploratory analysis.
